A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs present the same C-TRPO/C-NPG research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original results on eight Safety Gymnasium tasks, including baseline comparisons and parameter-sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original eight-task benchmark results, expanded baseline comparisons, and a CPO/C-TRPO hysteresis ablation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the recovery advantage from Ac to negative Ac, matching the cost-minimization instruction already present in v1's prose. The constrained geometry, surrogate update, C-NPG, and hysteresis mechanism are retained; this correction does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four locomotion and four navigation tasks from Safety Gymnasium, alongside the same two-state, two-action toy MDP. The new continuous-space discussion formalizes settings already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The main benchmark expands from five to nine safe-RL baselines by adding FOCOPS, CUP, IPO, and P3O. The individual-environment plots replace CPO with TRPO-Lag and P3O alongside PCPO. Unconstrained PPO is no longer tabulated in Table 1, although it remains the reward-normalization reference.

E3.justification: The new ablation introduces matched CPO/C-TRPO controls with and without hysteresis. V2 defines regret over training iterations instead of episodes and uses final-performance, IQM-based reporting where v1 specifies averages over post-training evaluations. The ten-million-step budget remains; these reporting revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds an eight-task ablation separating the effects of safe geometry and hysteresis (Appendix D.2, Figure 10), addressing whether hysteresis alone explains the advantage over CPO. The beta and hysteresis sensitivity plots are retained, but v1's cost-threshold sweep and two of its four toy-trajectory settings are removed.

E5.justification: V2's Table 1 adds lower and upper confidence intervals to per-task reward, cost, and regret results; v1's table reports point estimates. Five training seeds and aggregate stratified-bootstrap intervals already appear in v1. V2 no longer specifies v1's ten post-training evaluation runs, without establishing that their number decreased.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the per-task results, adds numerical regret entries and four baselines' scores, and reports new ablation outcomes. For example, Table 1 changes C-TRPO's AntVelocity reward/cost from 2736.1/6.1 to 3099.0/18.8. These are replaced reported results under revised endpoint reporting, not an established same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: V2 adds continuous-space occupancy and divergence definitions in Appendix B.3, generalizes cost regret across constraints, and explicitly assigns infinite surrogate divergence outside its domain. It also corrects the appendix's cost-value definition. The principal update bounds, safety and convergence statements, and proof strategies are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain safe policy-space geometry, C-TRPO and its C-NPG counterpart, theoretical safety/convergence guarantees, and competitive returns with fewer constraint violations. Rewriting and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablation as evidence that the geometry helps independently of hysteresis and attributes P3O's aggregate safety–reward tradeoff to conservative distance from the threshold. It removes the cost-threshold robustness interpretation and explicitly states that the theoretical analysis requires finite MDPs. Existing finite-sample and expected-cost safety limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies a Gaussian policy with a state-dependent mean network and parameterized, state-independent diagonal covariance, and supplies its closed-form KL expression. These document the existing continuous-control implementation rather than establish an architecture change. The promise to release code after review is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 expands the distinction between Lagrangian, fixed-penalty, and trust-region methods, adding references on regularization error, first-order constrained optimization, and Gaussian KL divergence. It replaces v1's unrelated Liu et al. 2021 citation for IPO with Liu et al. 2020's IPO paper and removes the Tomar et al. 2022 reference.

P1.justification: The introduction, method exposition, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. V2 introduces a separate C-NPG subsection, reorganizes implementation and proof material, and expands the background explanations. The performance-difference theorem moves from the main text to Appendix C.1, while several appendix discussions are regrouped.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout, adds introductory and CPO-comparison schematics, and adapts v1's Figure 1 into appendix Figure 5. It reduces and recolors the toy-trajectory figure, replaces aggregate training curves with grouped endpoint bars, adds an ablation figure, and transposes and expands Table 1 with regret and confidence intervals.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the empirical case by separating the geometry's contribution from hysteresis in Appendix D.2, evaluating relevant additional baselines, and reporting per-task uncertainty. These improve attribution and transparency. The loss of the cost-threshold robustness study offsets some gains, and practical finite-sample safety remains unanalyzed, making the overall improvement positive but limited.
